documents.title: Data centers are cropping up all over Bexar County with 23 more on the way
documents.publisher: San Antonio Report / Texas Public Radio
documents.text: More than 30 data centers are built in Bexar County and at least 23 more are on the way. Outside cities, many data centers face no zoning laws and can be built next to or within residential areas. Public Citizen, Sierra Club and the Environmental Integrity Project filed a July 22 complaint against two San Antonio data centers with on-site natural gas plants run by VoltaGrid, arguing they need major-source air permits. Deedee Belmares, clean energy advocate, Public Citizen: "They're able to cluster in the same area because they're able to utilize some of the same resources, like substations" Environmental Integrity Project press release, on the July 22 complaint about on-site gas plants at two Vantage data centers: "The developers are building 423 megawatts of dedicated generation capacity" Dan Diorio, Data Center Coalition: "Our member companies are already deploying advanced cooling technologies" Jeff Webster, Greater San Antonio Chamber of Commerce: "These projects represent significant capital investment in our community" Mayor Gina Ortiz Jones, San Antonio: "These companies aren't waiting on our timeline. We should proactively help ourselves." No Bexar County moratorium or county data-center rule is reported; Harlingen (Cameron County) adopted a 120-day moratorium.

events.title: Governor directs PUCT and ERCOT to audit data centers in the interconnection queue; ERCOT pauses Batch Zero
PUCT grants ERCOT good-cause exceptions for the audit timeline
Governor directs TCEQ to "halt all permits sought by data centers until the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) completes its audit"

approval.value: No zoning approval: Bexar County has no zoning authority outside cities. Expect county subdivision platting, floodplain development review and site permits.
approval.note: Texas counties have no general zoning authority (Tex. Loc. Gov. Code ch. 231), per Atria zoning jurisdiction. No published county timeline; verify with Bexar County Public Works.
